intro: Armenian and international outlets cover a range of political, diplomatic, and cultural developments, with particular focus on peace talks with Azerbaijan, the TRIPP project ratification, and Queen Sofía of Spain's visit to Armenian heritage sites.

topics.title: Armenia signals readiness to sign peace treaty with Azerbaijan by 2026
topics.text: Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan stated that Armenia is prepared to sign a peace treaty with Azerbaijan as early as 2026. He also noted that the return of Armenians held in Azerbaijan through third countries is not possible.

topics.title: Parliament ratifies TRIPP project agreement amid opposition objections
topics.text: Armenia's National Assembly ratified the Armenia-US framework agreement on the TRIPP project. Prime Minister Pashinyan urged the opposition to support putting the draft Constitution to a referendum and criticized calls for a guarantor for the project.

topics.title: Queen Sofía of Spain visits Armenian cultural and natural heritage sites
topics.text: Queen Sofía visited the Garni Temple, the 'Symphony of Stones' natural monument, and the Geghard Monastery during her trip to Armenia. COP17 delegates also toured historic and cultural monuments in the country.

topics.title: Robert Arzumanyan departs as Urartu head coach
topics.text: Robert Arzumanyan has left his position as head coach of FC Urartu. The Armenian national team is simultaneously preparing to compete at the 2026 IWF World Championships in weightlifting.

topics.title: Armenia expands economic ties with UAE and sees growth in EU clothing exports
topics.text: Armenia and the UAE ratified an agreement on trade, services, and investment expected to open new business opportunities. Meanwhile, Armenian-made clothing exports to the EU market increased by 17.2% year-over-year, and the Deputy PM discussed government priorities with the Asian Development Bank vice president.

topics.title: AMAA holds 107th annual meeting and honors community leaders in New Jersey
topics.text: The Armenian Missionary Association of America (AMAA) convened its 107th annual meeting in New Jersey, honoring Rev. Dr. Vahan H. Tootikian and Dr. Nurhan Helvacian. The Armenian Museum of America also highlighted renewed purpose in its mission.

topics.title: Yerevan addresses infrastructure challenges and sustainable development goals
topics.text: Deputy Prime Minister attributed Yerevan's water problems to ageing infrastructure. Prime Minister Pashinyan emphasized Armenia's commitment to the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the Montreal Declaration, while officials stressed coordinated efforts for environmental challenges.
